summary: Holistic session review passed after closing managed-image drift and release-workflow command-injection paths.

findings.description: Managed lifecycle actions validated channel resources but did not compare ANSWER_ENGINE_IMAGE with .release-state.json, so start, repair, stop, status, or uninstall could execute against a mutable or unrelated image while reporting the verified digest. Lifecycle ownership now requires a regular, valid release-state file and exact environment agreement, while allowing either side of a recorded pending transition so interrupted upgrades and rollbacks remain resumable.

The release workflow interpolated runtime_image directly into shell source after validating only an unanchored digest suffix, allowing a crafted workflow-dispatch value to inject commands on the candidate runner. Release inputs now pass through environment variables, the runtime image is anchored to the official content-addressed repository, and the standalone asset builder enforces the same identity.
